Mike Stearman was unlucky in the fact that owing to arriving a bit late he missed the start and trailed the field along and so can be said to have done well to finish 41st out of the 63 who completed the course.

Brian Trower was 37th, with Mike Stearman 40th, and Mike was another just getting over the 'flu, and then came Don McLean, 65. We were pleased to see Geoff Goode out once again, and he looked short of training and has also put on quite a bit of weight in the Army.
The handicap was won by Mike Stearman (4.30) with Stan Gawler (3.30) 2nd and D.
Gawler and Mike Stearman all of whom were to give the selectors some head aches when trying to find the best team for the approaching National Brighton Relay.

Don Maclean was untroubled for the greater part and ran a very well-judged race. It was very good to see Gordan Biscoe and Mike Stearman out again, as it was to see such an encouraging performance from John Hilton.

Mike Stearman, now turning out regularly for us was 5th in a classy 3 mile field. Young D.Cocks showed his class once more by taking the Youths 880 yards in 2:07.8, with his comrade-in-arms, Pottinger setting about the field events with an excellent 36ft 7½inch H.S.J., followed by a 35'11" shot-putt.

Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman.

A further gap followed before Dennis Jones appeared 83rd, John Collier 90th and Mike Stearman 92nd. Don Maclean was having one of his days and was lying 120th and Alan Bishop completed our contingent in 125th place.

Mike Stearman who had come only as a supporter, was press-ganged into running the last leg after 5 months of inactivity! His fine effort in a complete set of borrowed kit (by no means fresh!) enabled us to finish 5th out of 12 teams.

The start was fairly fast with first Mike Stearman and then Eric Gebbett enjoying a brief few seconds of glory. By 600 yards however Charlie Dabbs was in command with a fair sized bunch of runners all lying handy.
Those who rarely miss a fixture include George Piddington, Chris Fairfield Dennis Jones, Eric Penny and Mike Stearman, with another half-dozen not far behind.
Joe Dooley produced some strong running over the last 2 miles and gained four places. Mike Stearman won the handicap and Pat Newell's excellent run earned him second place from scratch.

His struggling effort left him over two minutes behind our first man, Peter Whewell, and dangerously near that old Belgrave favourite, Jack Brown. It was good to see Mike Stearman out in the "Open" running again.
In the Belgrave Handicap,"old-stagers" Don Maclean and Mike Stearman tied for first place Third was that scourge of the handicapper, Jim Rimmer - he'll have his wings removed altogether soon!
'Old man' Mike Stearman on the come-back trail showed he meant business by giving Pat O'Connor a few uncomfortable moments and some of these watching food for thought.
